messages:
Alex: quick heads-up — I pushed an experiment to staging: compactification for signal cards. it collapses high-frequency SLO hits into a single card with routing hints. want quick feedback on API shape + routing semantics
Sam: nice, can you paste the example payload? curious how tenant attribution looks when we coalesce events
Alex: sure — snippet we used in the runner:
```json
{"compact_rules": [{"window_seconds": 300, "collapse_by": ["tenant_id","signal_hash"], "severity_rank": ["P0","P1","P2"], "route_policy": "dominant"}], "emit_meta": true}
```
Priya: so in "dominant" route_policy we pick the highest-severity route that's present across collapsed events? or earliest? we need deterministic tie-breaker
Alex: currently dominant picks highest severity, then most recent, then lowest latency route. we can change but wanted to test the UX first
Dana: my main worry is notifications: if we aggregate, do we still fanout to multiple escalation paths? some customers expect separate pagers for separate failing tenants
Alex: good point. current shim emits a single console card + a routing_summary array, we then expand to multiple notifications only if `route_policy: fanout_on_distinct_escalations`
Mei: can we get a sample of the routing_summary shape? need to wire into notify-preview panel for the console
Alex: example:
```json
"routing_summary": [{"route":"oncall-ops","count":3,"severity":"P1"},{"route":"tenant-owner:acme","count":1,"severity":"P0"}]
```
Jonah: sounds reasonable. two UX asks: 1) show collapsed count prominently, 2) let user toggle "explode" to see constituent events and quick re-run evals
Priya: +1 on toggle. also we should include an aggregate error-budget delta so owners know if this collapse hides multiple small burns vs one big outage
Alex: we included `budget_impact` in meta — integer of 1e-6 units to keep it small. console shows normalized percent.
ProductOps: are we confident about noise/alert fatigue improvements? customers will be nervous if we hide alerts by default. maybe make compact mode opt-in per tenant first
Sam: defaults: opt-out for enterprise tier? or start with an experimental flag in console rollout (beta label)
Dana: telemetry question — when collapsed, do we lose per-token traces? we need to ensure event ids still map back to traces for postmortem
Alex: no loss — we store an array `constituent_ids` with pointers to the original events, GUIDs. also instrumented a `reconstruct()` call in the internal API: `POST /v1/compact/reconstruct {compact_id}` returns full event list
Mei: okay great. that reconstruct API will be what notify-preview calls when user clicks "explode"
Jonah: routing contract nit: when route_policy: dominant but dominant route is rate-limited or snoozed, do we fallback to next route or queue?
Alex: current plan: fallback chain based on severity fallback table. we add a `fallback_applied` boolean in routing_summary entries to make it auditable
Priya: can we add a small simulation mode in the API? like `dry_run=true` that returns what notifications would have been sent without mutating counters
Alex: yes implementing `dry_run` now — `GET /v1/compact/simulate?compact_payload=...` returns `simulated_notifications` and `simulated_budget_impact`
ProductOps: rollout plan idea: 1) internal beta on staging, 2) permitlist a few tenants, 3) soft default in console with explicit "Enable compact view" CTA, 4) measure change in notify volume and MTTA
Sam: we'll need new telemetry: per-tenant compact_rate, expand_click_rate, avg_delta_in_notifications, percent_fallbacks. also SLA for reconstruct latency (<200ms typical)
Dana: and a safety: if reconstruct API fails, UI should surface an error and default to non-compact expanded view to avoid mystery
